standard.title: Modifications for inclusion
standard.description: investigate modifications to equipment, rules and scoring systems that support fair play and inclusive participation
standard.prior_knowledge: Students have devised and tested alternative rules and game modifications to support fair play and inclusive participation (Y5-6). They have tested modifications but have not yet systematically investigated how and why modifications work.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students investigate modifications to equipment, rules and scoring systems that support fair play and inclusive participation.

nodes.label: Understanding fair play and inclusion as design criteria
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can explain what fair play and inclusive participation mean in a physical activity context and identify specific conditions that threaten or support them.
nodes.minimum_width: Explain what fair play and inclusive participation mean and identify one condition in a physical activity that threatens either.
nodes.typical_width: Explain fair play and inclusion as design criteria; identify a range of conditions (equipment, skill gaps, rule complexity, physical ability) that can threaten or support each; explain how scoring systems can be structured to advantage or disadvantage different participant groups.
wider: Analyse the benefits and potential drawbacks of player-officiated games where players rather than an independent official are responsible for officiating, examining how this affects fair play
Explore how traditional games of First Nations Australians are structured to support fair play and inclusive participation, identifying the design principles underlying these structures
nodes.hinge_reason: Without understanding fair play and inclusion as criteria, modification investigations become arbitrary rather than purposeful. Students need to know what they are designing for before they can evaluate whether modifications achieve it.

response_modes.reason: Explicitly establish fair play and inclusion as design criteria with concrete indicators before investigation begins. Ask students to identify who is disadvantaged in a given game and what the modification is trying to fix.

success_criteria: Explains what fair play means in a physical activity context
Explains what inclusive participation means and gives one example of a condition that limits it

nodes.label: Investigating modification types
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can investigate specific modifications to equipment, rules or scoring systems and explain how each modification is intended to support fair play or inclusive participation.
nodes.minimum_width: Investigate one modification (equipment, rules or scoring) and explain how it is intended to support fair play or inclusive participation.
nodes.typical_width: Investigate a range of modifications across all three types (equipment, rules, scoring); apply and adapt scoring systems to assess movement performances consistently and fairly; examine how modifications interact and whether they create new inequities.
wider: Explore rules, equipment and scoring systems of traditional games of First Nations Australians, investigating how they support skill development and fair and inclusive play

Research how modified sport programs (e.g. sitting volleyball, bocce, Auslan volleyball) have been designed to extend participation, comparing the design principles to those used in class game modifications

response_modes.reason: Investigation across all three modification types (equipment, rules, scoring) builds a complete toolkit — students who have only investigated one type have an incomplete picture of how game design supports inclusion.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: First Nations game design principles and modified sport research connect modification investigation to broader cultural and design literacy — students who engage here build genuine understanding of inclusive design as a principled discipline.
success_criteria: Investigates at least one modification and explains how it is intended to support fair play or inclusive participation
Identifies which modification type (equipment, rules, or scoring) the modification belongs to

nodes.label: Applying and evaluating modifications
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can apply modifications in practice and evaluate their effectiveness at supporting fair play and inclusive participation, identifying strengths and limitations.
nodes.minimum_width: Apply one modification in a physical activity and evaluate whether it achieved its intended purpose, giving one reason.
nodes.typical_width: Apply and evaluate modifications across multiple activity contexts; assess whether modifications enable all participants to experience success; identify unintended consequences; propose refinements based on evaluation findings.
wider: Modify rules, equipment or scoring systems from scratch for a specific group with particular participation needs, testing and evaluating the design against inclusion criteria through multiple iterations
Analyse a player-officiated game context and evaluate how the absence of an independent official affects both fair play and inclusive participation dynamics

response_modes.reason: Applying and evaluating modifications integrates design criteria understanding, modification knowledge and reflective evaluation. The evaluation must circle back to the original design criteria — fair play and inclusive participation — not just satisfaction or enjoyment.

success_criteria: Applies at least one modification in a physical activity
Evaluates whether the modification achieved its intended purpose (fair play or inclusive participation)
Identifies at least one strength and one limitation of the modification
